amd_9950x.note: 16 physical cores, SMT siblings excluded. Measured, not assumed: benchmark/results/THREAD-SWEEP-AMD9950X.md sweeps 4-32 threads and finds the joint optimum at 16 for both engines, with llama.cpp prefill collapsing ~6x under SMT. Decode uses 15 by the core-minus-one rule; that specific value sits on the 12-16 plateau but was not measured on its own.

apple_temp_gate.note: Every run starts on a cool chip (#17, benchmark/METHODOLOGY.md#cool-start-on-apple-silicon): the same rule as the Metal profile, here on the CPU temperature, which an 8-thread prefill drives as hard as Metal drives the GPU. Measured on the M1 Max (2026-10-21, macmon): idle under the lock the chip settles at GPU 49-55 C, CPU 50-55 C; Metal prefill takes the GPU from 49 to 76 C in 7 s, the clock leaves 1293 MHz at 78-83 C and the GPU reaches 96 C after 90 s; from there it is back below 65 C in about 40 s and below 60 C in about 75 s (CPU alike). Without macmon the gate pauses 45 s instead and records cool_gate=time.

host_gate.note: Replaces the load-average test on this host (bench_cross_engine.py host_is_quiet): macOS on an interactive desktop shared with agents never shows a load average near 0.2/core (2026-10-12: 4-8 at 73 % idle), so the frozen gate waited out Gitea's 3 h job limit without one measurement. The host is quiet when >= 80 % of all cores stayed idle over the settle window; the other agents' benchmarks are excluded by ~/bin/with-mac-lock. A run whose repeats spread by more than 5 % (prefill or decode, any length) is discarded and measured again, up to 3 times: the gate before a run cannot see work that starts during it. A cell waits at most 20 min for a quiet host and then fails as busy: Gitea hands the macOS runner its jobs in ID order, so a nightly cell waiting 2 h per cycle on a desktop in use held every macOS CI check behind it for a day (2026-10-13).
